body: INDEPENDENT FULL READ — AMEND exact off-tree SHA-256 ec1f308fecdb5f84f473818e4e1667f67ca04ae4dff6e808ef79b7ae5491dfba, 1,048 lines, 8,357 words, 62,864 bytes. The prior decoded-progress, C2 boundary, atomic-exclusive publication, owner-bound no-JavaScript, and external-resource repairs all pass. One exact internal contradiction remains. Section 2.1 lines 29-34 permits inline SVG and forbids CSS URLs only when they load bytes outside preview.html. C10 line 920 says adding any `url(...)` to inline CSS fails. That broader court also rejects a self-contained same-document `url(#local-id)` reference, which is the ordinary inline-SVG mechanism for hatch patterns, markers, masks, filters, and clip paths. It can therefore prohibit the very non-colour structural marks the report contract permits without loading any external bytes. Minimal repair: make the negative mutation an externally resolving URL such as `url(https://invalid.example/x)` and a sibling-relative `url(asset.svg#x)`, while adding a positive same-document `url(#local-id)` inline-SVG control. If data URLs are intentionally forbidden, state that as a separately justified canonical-profile restriction rather than deriving it from no external resources. Everything else in this digest passes my blocker-class review, including O1 standoff, O2 role-separated roots, O3 two-tier spike, O4 report-not-parser, complete text twins, cross-root closure, and post-commit outcome honesty. No implementation, public-name, dependency, candidate, or landing authority follows.
